output.brief: The rejections most likely come from our own shipping data, not the fungicide, the growers, or the carrier. After the move to the Tallis system on 1 August, the product record for mandarins (PRD-MAND-01) was copied from an avocado record and carries a 7.0°C carriage temperature instead of our specified 4.0°C. Every rejected container was booked through Tallis at 7°C. The four Pellacor-era containers booked at 4°C passed, and a container with the old fungicide at 7°C was rejected. Meridane's controllers held their set points, so a refrigeration claim is not supported. I am fairly confident in this. The records do not yet show the link to decay for every container, and the growers' share of fruit is similar in passing and failing containers. Next: correct PRD-MAND-01 to 4°C now, and ask Meridane to reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 October. Check every booking against the specification before sending. Hold off on the Lower Serra suspension, the fungicide change, the Brindle deduction, and the Meridane claim. Consider independent loggers as a cheap check.
